arxiv-1702-02717.title: A Characterisation of Smooth Maps into a Homogeneous Space
arxiv-1702-02717.creator: Anthony D. BLAOM
arxiv-1702-02717.description: Abstract We generalize Cartan’s logarithmic derivative of a smooth map from a manifold into a Lie group G G to smooth maps into a homogeneous space M = G / H M=G/H , and determine the global monodromy obstruction to reconstructing such maps from infinitesimal data.

arxiv-2106-12333.title: Packing theory derived from phyllotaxis and products of linear forms
arxiv-2106-12333.creator: S. E. Graiff Zurita, B. Kane, R. Oishi-Tomiyasu
arxiv-2106-12333.description: Abstract Parastichies are spiral patterns observed in plants and numerical patterns generated using golden angle method. We generalize this method by using Markoff theory and the theory of product of linear forms, to obtain a theory for packing of Riemannian manifolds of general dimensions n n with a locally diagonalizable metric, including the Euclidean spaces.

arxiv-2203-06370.title: On smooth plane models for modular curves of Shimura type
arxiv-2203-06370.creator: Samuele Anni, Eran Assaf, Elisa Lorenzo García
arxiv-2203-06370.description: Abstract . In this paper we prove that there are finitely many modular curves that admit a smooth plane model. Moreover, if the degree of the model is greater than or equal to 19 19 , no such curve exists.

arxiv-2208-09853.title: Quantifying chaos using Lagrangian descriptors
arxiv-2208-09853.creator: M. Hillebrand, S. Zimper, A. Ngapasare, M. Katsanikas, S. Wiggins, Ch. Skokos
arxiv-2208-09853.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by M. Hillebrand, S. Zimper, A. Ngapasare, M. Katsanikas, S. Wiggins, Ch. Skokos. We present and validate simple and efficient methods to estimate the chaoticity of orbits in low-dimensional conservative dynamical systems, namely autonomous Hamiltonian systems and area-preserving symplectic maps, from computations of Lagrangian descriptors (LDs) on short time scales.

arxiv-2301-11553.title: Robust Transformer with Locality Inductive Bias and Feature Normalization
arxiv-2301-11553.creator: Omid Nejati Manzari, Hossein Kashiani, Hojat Asgarian Dehkordi, Shahriar Baradaran Shokouhi
arxiv-2301-11553.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Omid Nejati Manzari, Hossein Kashiani, Hojat Asgarian Dehkordi, Shahriar Baradaran Shokouhi. Vision transformers have been demonstrated to yield state-of-the-art results on a variety of computer vision tasks using attention-based networks. However, research works in transformers mostly do not investigate robustness/accuracy trade-off, and they still struggle to handle adversarial perturbations. In this paper, we explore the robustness of vision transformers against adversarial perturbations and try to enhance their robustness/accuracy trade-off in white box attack settings.

arxiv-2304-03494.title: Exploiting Alternating DVS Shot Noise Event Pair Statistics to Reduce Background Activity Rates Thanks: RG supported by Swiss National Science Foundation grant SCIDVS (200021_185069).
arxiv-2304-03494.creator: Brian McReynolds, Rui Graca, Tobi Delbruck
arxiv-2304-03494.description: Abstract Dynamic Vision Sensors (DVS) record ”events” corresponding to pixel-level brightness changes, resulting in data-efficient representation of a dynamic visual scene. As DVS expand into increasingly diverse applications, non-ideal behaviors in their output under extreme sensing conditions are important to consider.

arxiv-2305-17300.title: Exploiting Large Neuroimaging Datasets to Create Connectome-Constrained Approaches for more Robust, Efficient, and Adaptable Artificial Intelligence
arxiv-2305-17300.creator: Erik C. Johnson, Brian S. Robinson, Gautam K. Vallabha, Justin Joyce, Jordan K. Matelsky
arxiv-2305-17300.description: Abstract Despite the progress in deep learning networks, efficient learning at the edge (enabling adaptable, low-complexity machine learning solutions) remains a critical need for defense and commercial applications. We have pursued multiple neuroscience-inspired AI efforts which may overcome these data inefficiencies, power inefficiencies, and lack of generalization.

arxiv-2406-20034.title: Tense logics based on posets
arxiv-2406-20034.creator: Ivan Chajda 1,5 , Helmut Länger 2,6 , Antonio Ledda 3,7 , Jan Paseka 4,6 and Gandolfo Vergottini 3
arxiv-2406-20034.description: Abstract . Not all logical systems can be captured using algebras. We see this in classical logic (formalized by Boolean algebras) and many-valued logics (like Łukasiewicz logic with MV-algebras). Even quantum mechanics, initially formalized with orthomodular lattices, benefits from a simpler approach using just partially ordered sets (posets). This paper explores how logical connectives are introduced in poset-based logics.

arxiv-2503-04652.title: Evaluation of Privacy-aware Support Vector Machine (SVM) Learning using Homomorphic Encryption
arxiv-2503-04652.creator: William J Buchanan, Hisham Ali
arxiv-2503-04652.description: Abstract The requirement for privacy-aware machine learning increases as we continue to use PII (Personally Identifiable Information) within machine training. To overcome these privacy issues, we can apply Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) to encrypt data before it is fed into a machine learning model.

arxiv-2506-19699.title: UniTac-NV: A Unified Tactile Representation For Non-Vision-Based Tactile Sensors*
arxiv-2506-19699.creator: Jian Hou, Xin Zhou, Qihan Yang, and Adam J. Spiers
arxiv-2506-19699.description: Abstract Generalizable algorithms for tactile sensing remain underexplored, primarily due to the diversity of sensor modalities. Recently, many methods for cross-sensor transfer between optical (vision-based) tactile sensors have been investigated, yet little work focus on non-optical tactile sensors. To address this gap, we propose an encoder-decoder architecture to unify tactile data across non-vision-based sensors.

arxiv-2510-12286.title: Train Stochastic Non Linear Coupled ODEs to Classify and Generate
arxiv-2510-12286.creator: Stefano Gagliani 1 , Feliciano Giuseppe Pacifico 1,2 , Lorenzo Chicchi 1 , Duccio Fanelli 1 , Diego Febbe 1 , Lorenzo Buffoni 1 , Raffaele Marino 1
arxiv-2510-12286.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Stefano Gagliani 1 , Feliciano Giuseppe Pacifico 1,2 , Lorenzo Chicchi 1 , Duccio Fanelli 1 , Diego Febbe 1 , Lorenzo Buffoni 1 , Raffaele Marino 1. A general class of dynamical systems which can be trained to operate in classification and generation modes are introduced. A procedure is proposed to plant asymptotic stationary attractors of the deterministic model.

pmc-10746107.creator: Jack Syage, Ana Ramos, Vasiliy Loskutov, Anna Norum, Adam Bledsoe, Rok Seon Choung, Matthew Dickason, Jennifer Sealey-Voyksner, Joseph Murray, Carlo Catassi, Fernando Chirdo

pmc-11472085.description: Improving yield via assessment of different yield-related genetic parameters specifically with the challenges of yield × traits combination is a prominent issue for plant breeders. A graphical and numerical description of diallel analysis by yield × traits with the novelty of the parent selection with desirable genetic architecture in rapeseed was illustrated via Hayman and biplot approaches.

pmc-12378795.title: Current landscape of the immunoproteasome: implications for disease and therapy
pmc-12378795.creator: Zifeng Zou, Yanglin Hao, Zetong Tao, Weicong Ye, Zilong Luo, Xiaohan Li, Ran Li, Kexiao Zheng, Jiahong Xia, Chao Guo, Xi Zhang, Jie Wu
pmc-12378795.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The immunoproteasome, an inflammation-induced proteasome variant, coordinates proteostasis and adaptive immunity by replacing constitutive subunits (β1, β2, β5) with inducible counterparts (β1i, β2i, β5i). This specialization enhances antigen processing for MHC class I presentation and oxidative protein clearance. Beyond immune regulation, it critically contributes to cardiovascular, respiratory, neurodegenerative, autoimmune, retinal, and oncological pathologies through mechanisms involving NF-κB activation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and inflammatory polarization.

pmc-13605357.title: Quantitative MRI Volumetry as a Potential Neuroimaging Biomarker in Levetiracetam-Treated Epilepsy
pmc-13605357.creator: Sibel Çıplak, Serkan Ünlü
pmc-13605357.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: Quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) volumetry may provide an objective approach for detecting subtle longitudinal structural brain changes in patients with epilepsy. This retrospective longitudinal study investigated regional and global brain volume changes observed during levetiracetam (LEV) monotherapy. Methods: Thirty-seven adults with epilepsy who underwent brain MRI before initiation of LEV monotherapy (MRI-1) and approximately 12 months later (MRI-2) were included. Automated volumetric segmentation was performed using volBrain, and within-subject changes in macrostructural, subcortical, and cortical volumes were evaluated.
